original_test_intent: Read the intended BMC's Redfish Role collection, validate its identity, member graph and approved privilege definitions, and preserve a controlled authorization-policy snapshot without changing roles.
original_method: Retain one GET to `/redfish/v1/AccountService/Roles`, replacing embedded credentials and TLS bypass with trusted least-privilege access, then validate collection and permitted member metadata against policy.
manual_activity: The security/BMC owner approves the credential and transport trust, supplies the expected role/privilege baseline, and defines which role identifiers, privilege arrays, OEM fields and account associations may be exported.
required_inputs: BMC endpoint bound to immutable SUT identity
safety_requirements: Do not expose credentials or Authorization
Do not resolve members outside the advertised Roles namespace
No role, privilege, account or password mutation
agent_execution_scope: Bind endpoint and certificate to intended BMC
Issue one bounded Roles collection GET
Validate RoleCollection identity, count and unique member links
Compare privilege arrays and OEM extensions to baseline
Export redacted policy snapshot and no-mutation audit
engineer_actions: Approve access and authorized member-resolution depth
Provide role/privilege baseline and redaction rules

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The GET endpoint matches the source, but `-k`, basic-auth argv and unredacted full JSON are unsafe; readability does not validate collection consistency or privilege policy.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: With trusted TLS and secret-safe least-privilege authentication, GET the Roles collection once, validate collection identity/count/unique links, resolve only approved role members, compare privilege sets to the authorized baseline and export redacted evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The exact Roles path, GET intent and 15/10 timing remain; no expected roles, privilege arrays or OEM extensions are inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat the Roles endpoint as an authorization-policy graph: reconcile count with unique in-namespace member links, validate each approved Role resource, and compare privileges/OEM definitions to a signed baseline.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds trusted transport, schema, graph integrity, policy comparison and controlled disclosure instead of full-JSON readability.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A collection GET alone proves neither each role's privileges nor policy conformance; member resolution is bounded and does not authorize any PATCH.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Role names and privilege combinations reveal security posture. Vendor-defined roles or OEM privileges need an explicit baseline and must not be normalized into standard roles by guesswork.

project_override_considerations: A Redfish client library is equivalent only if it preserves certificate verification, least privilege, collection/count/link invariants, exact privilege-array comparison and approved redaction; vendor pagination/OEM roles require explicit profile support.
expected_evidence: Credential-provider and schema/parser versions without secrets
HTTP status/content type and access-controlled raw response hash
RoleCollection @odata identity, count and unique in-namespace links
Approved role-member schemas and exact privilege/OEM comparison
No role, privilege, account, password or log change

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item, procedure, path and DeepSeek command consistently specify a GET of the Roles collection. Security omissions and weak criteria do not create a source contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The read endpoint is explicit. Trust, access, schemas, privilege baseline and redaction are obtainable project prerequisites.

review_improvement: Converts a readable Roles dump into a trusted, count-consistent and baseline-compared authorization-policy inventory with controlled disclosure.
independent_technical_reasoning: A valid Roles collection must reconcile its reported count with unique member links confined to the expected namespace. Policy correctness then depends on exact privilege arrays and any OEM additions for each approved role, not merely role labels or successful JSON parsing. Because this data maps authorization capability, the raw response must be access-controlled and the export redacted; the neighboring PATCH case remains wholly outside this GET scope.
